heading_path: Buyer's Guide Manage payments - Financial claims
blocks.markdown: ## Financial claims
blocks.plain_text: Financial claims

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Manage payments - Financial claims
blocks.markdown: This section provides guidelines for managing financial claims related to contracts. By understanding these procedures, you can protect Canada's financial interests and ensure compliance with all relevant policies and directives. This includes handling claims for extra payments by contractors and managing financial claims owed to Canada.
blocks.plain_text: This section provides guidelines for managing financial claims related to contracts. By understanding these procedures, you can protect Canada's financial interests and ensure compliance with all relevant policies and directives. This includes handling claims for extra payments by contractors and managing financial claims owed to Canada.

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Manage payments - Financial claims
blocks.markdown: ### Claims for extra payment
blocks.plain_text: Claims for extra payment

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Manage payments - Financial claims
blocks.markdown: Contractors may occasionally submit claims for increased payments for firm price contracts due to changes caused by Canada. A firm price contract may not be amended for upward price revision without prior approval of Treasury Board (TB), unless the contract specifically includes an escalation clause, covering the adjustment requested or the contract conditions allowed for the requested adjustment.
blocks.plain_text: Contractors may occasionally submit claims for increased payments for firm price contracts due to changes caused by Canada. A firm price contract may not be amended for upward price revision without prior approval of Treasury Board (TB), unless the contract specifically includes an escalation clause, covering the adjustment requested or the contract conditions allowed for the requested adjustment.

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Manage payments - Financial claims
blocks.markdown: TB approval is mandatory for all claims of extra payment, regardless of the amount involved. Typically, TB will not approve extra payment claims that result solely from:
blocks.plain_text: TB approval is mandatory for all claims of extra payment, regardless of the amount involved. Typically, TB will not approve extra payment claims that result solely from:

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Manage payments - Financial claims
blocks.markdown:
- labor or material cost increases
- changes in freight rates
- exchange rate revisions
- contractor-caused delays
- errors on the part of the contractor
- other difficulties that the contractor overlooked, but should have foreseen
blocks.plain_text: labor or material cost increases ; changes in freight rates ; exchange rate revisions ; contractor-caused delays ; errors on the part of the contractor ; other difficulties that the contractor overlooked, but should have foreseen

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Manage payments - Financial claims
blocks.markdown: You should consult Legal Services to determine if the extra payment constitutes a contract amendment or an "ex gratia" payment.
blocks.plain_text: You should consult Legal Services to determine if the extra payment constitutes a contract amendment or an "ex gratia" payment.

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Manage payments - Financial claims
blocks.markdown: The TB has granted full authority to deputy heads to make "ex gratia" payments and to designate officials within the department to act on their behalf. See the TB Directive on Payments.
blocks.plain_text: The TB has granted full authority to deputy heads to make "ex gratia" payments and to designate officials within the department to act on their behalf. See the TB Directive on Payments.

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Manage payments - Financial claims
blocks.markdown: When monies may be owing to Canada from contracting activities, it is essential to determine the liability and amount owing with assistance, as necessary from Legal Services.
blocks.plain_text: When monies may be owing to Canada from contracting activities, it is essential to determine the liability and amount owing with assistance, as necessary from Legal Services.

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Manage payments - Financial claims
blocks.markdown: There are special procedures to be followed whenever there are suggestions of unreasonably high profits from any contract pursuant to the Defence Production Act or from any contract other than a competitive firm priced contract.
blocks.plain_text: There are special procedures to be followed whenever there are suggestions of unreasonably high profits from any contract pursuant to the Defence Production Act or from any contract other than a competitive firm priced contract.

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Manage payments - Financial claims
blocks.markdown: There are two general categories of claims by Canada related to contracting activities:

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Manage payments - Financial claims
blocks.markdown:
- overpayments or overclaims identified through an audit
- legal disputes, including termination for default or bankruptcy when the amount owed is known and final

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Manage payments - Financial claims
blocks.markdown: Note: Either instance can only be determined when a contract has been completed or terminated.

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Manage payments - Financial claims
blocks.markdown: You should coordinate with the contractor to obtain concurrence on the final amount owing. After determining this amount, you must instruct the client to establish an accounts receivable. The client must notify you that it has been done and initiate collection efforts.

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Manage payments - Financial claims

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Manage payments - Financial claims
blocks.markdown: Throughout the assurance engagement, all key stakeholders collaborate closely and maintain regular communication. This includes the assurance advisor, who provides guidance on assurance-related matters, the auditor team conducting the engagement, the PSPC buyer who manages the contract, the client and, when applicable, the price advisor, who was involved in negotiating the pricing arrangements for the contracts under examination.

- non-compliance with contract terms and conditions, Canada’s Contract Cost Principles 1031-2 and the Profit Principles (section 5.2 of the Practitioner’s Guide for Procurement Pricing )
- billing errors resulting from incorrect rates, quantities or invoiced amounts
- profit variance in excess of authorized contract profit

blocks.markdown: #### Notification report

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Manage payments - Financial claims
blocks.markdown: A notification report is initiated, drafted and prepared by the ASG. assurance advisor. It is prepared to outline the findings and recommended actions in dealing with the contractor’s claims for payment or excess profit, its accounting practices, or it’s internal controls.
blocks.plain_text: A notification report is initiated, drafted and prepared by the ASG. assurance advisor. It is prepared to outline the findings and recommended actions in dealing with the contractor’s claims for payment or excess profit, its accounting practices, or it’s internal controls.

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Manage payments - Financial claims
blocks.markdown: This report summarizes the results of the assurance engagement report and provides advice on the actions required by government representatives to mitigate the risk of overpayment on current and future contracts. The engagement report contains the full details of the assurance engagement results.

blocks.markdown: The notification report is intended to support buyers in the following areas:

heading_path: Buyer's Guide Manage payments - Financial claims
blocks.markdown:

- follow-up on matters of offeror compliance, as it relates to records, internal controls, cost accounting or billing practices
- documentation and approval of the disposition of findings raised in the assurance engagement report
- strategic decision-making, including modification to the basis of payment, clarifying terms and conditions of contracts, and modifications in costing methodology.
